issues.legal_issue: A consumer complaint may proceed in a representative capacity only where its pleadings and requested reliefs establish that the numerous consumers represented have the same interest.
material_facts: The complainants sought to represent purchasers of about 1,134 apartments, although none of the purchasers in one of the three blocks had joined and the complaint did not plead that block’s completion timeline.
The complaint did not specifically plead how purchasers in the other two blocks shared the same interest.
The period of delay could differ between purchasers, and purchasers differed in whether they accepted offered compensation, accepted it under protest, or refused it.
The requested delay compensation depended on the circumstances of each purchaser; some purchasers had also pursued separate grievances.
issues.conclusion: The permission to file the complaint in a representative capacity for all purchasers should not have been granted. The complaint is to be treated as a joint complaint by the complainants, not as a representative complaint for all purchasers.
issues.legal_principle: Section 35(1)(c) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 requires numerous consumers to have the same interest; Section 38(11) applies Order I Rule 8 CPC. Under the Explanation to Order I Rule 8, sameness of interest is distinct from sameness of cause of action: a shared cause of action alone does not establish shared interest. The pleadings and reliefs must be considered. Chairman, Tamil Nadu Housing Board v. T.N. Ganapathy was distinguishable because the challenged demand there was uniform and the decision was limited to a particular group of allottees. Rameshwar Prasad Shrivastava, Anjum Hussain and Vikrant Singh Malik were also considered in explaining the requirements for representative consumer complaints.

predicates.consumer_representative_case: One or more consumers seek to pursue a complaint on behalf of, or for the benefit of, numerous other consumers.
predicates.pleadings_establish_shared_interest: The complaint’s pleadings and requested reliefs establish that the consumers represented share an interest in the matter.

issues.definition: When consumers seek representative relief but the pleadings and requested reliefs do not establish their shared interest, representative permission is denied.

issues.legal_issue: Consumers may join in a complaint to seek redress for their own grievances without satisfying the requirements for a representative complaint on behalf of numerous consumers.
material_facts: Ninety-one consumers joined in filing the complaint and sought relief for themselves as well as for other purchasers.
The representative application was not maintainable, but the complainants had their own grievances arising from delayed possession.
The complaint could therefore continue as a joint complaint confined to the complainants, rather than being dismissed altogether.
issues.conclusion: The complaint remains maintainable as a joint complaint by the complainants for their own grievances, notwithstanding the failure of the representative basis.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 2(5), 35(1)(a) and 35(1)(c) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 distinguish a complaint by consumers for their own redress from one brought for numerous consumers. Section 38(11) applies Order I Rule 8 CPC to representative complaints, not to every complaint joined by multiple consumers. Section 13(2) of the General Clauses Act, 1897 provides that the singular includes the plural unless the context requires otherwise. Section 100 of the Consumer Protection Act does not exclude the principle in Order I Rule 1 CPC permitting persons to join as plaintiffs.

predicates.consumer_complaint: Consumers have filed a complaint seeking redress in relation to goods or services.
predicates.multiple_consumers_seek_own_redress: More than one consumer joins the complaint to seek relief for their own grievances.
predicates.representative_basis_unavailable: The complaint cannot proceed as a representative complaint on behalf of numerous consumers.

issues.definition: A consumer complaint joined by multiple consumers for their own redress may proceed as a joint complaint when its representative basis is unavailable.

issues.legal_issue: A consumer seeking to join an existing joint complaint may be added as a party when that consumer’s grievance is limited to the grievance presented in the complaint.
material_facts: Other purchasers applied to join the complaint after representative-capacity notices had been issued.
The intervenors’ stated grievance was within the grievance projected by the complainants in their complaint.
issues.conclusion: Consumers wishing to join may be added if their grievance is limited to the grievance projected in the complaint; the intervenors were to be impleaded.
issues.legal_principle: The Court directed that purchasers may join the complaint if their grievance is limited to the grievance projected by the complainants. The direction preserves the complaint as a joint complaint rather than extending it to represent consumers with different grievances.

predicates.joint_consumer_complaint: A complaint is proceeding as a joint complaint by consumers for their own grievances.
predicates.applicant_seeks_to_join: A consumer applies to become a party to the complaint.
predicates.applicant_grievance_matches_complaint: The applicant’s grievance is limited to the grievance presented in the complaint.

issues.definition: A consumer seeking to join a joint complaint may be added when that consumer’s grievance matches the grievance presented in the complaint.
